basis.statement: Observed choice treatment: X is generated from Q and its own noise in the simulated process; nothing assigns it. Observational design: back-door identification requires conditional exchangeability under the recorded graph, together with consistency, no interference and adequate overlap.
The graph “Simulated five-variable process” (revision 4e2cc0df) states the causes of X and Y; a missing arrow claims there is no direct cause.
No unmeasured common cause of X and Y remains after adjusting for Q. Test sensitivity to this assumption in the sensitivity chapter.
Consistency: each recorded treatment value represents one well-defined intervention, and a unit’s observed outcome equals its potential outcome under the treatment it received.
No interference: one unit’s treatment does not affect another unit’s outcome.
Adjusting for Q satisfies the back-door criterion for the total effect of X on Y: all 3 back-door paths are blocked, and no mediator, collider or post-treatment variable is adjusted for.
P is left out of the adjustment set: a collider; adjusting would open a path.
Back-door path X ← Q → Y is blocked at Q.
Path X → P ← Y is blocked at collider P, which is left alone.
Back-door path X ← Q ← S → Y is blocked at Q, S.
